intro.title: Build BFF endpoint aggregating multiple services
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) endpoint in Node.js that aggregates data from multiple mock services into a single response. You'll learn how to use the `async/await` syntax to handle asynchronous operations, making your code clean and readable. The main technologies involved are the built-in Node.js `https` module for making HTTP requests and Express.js for creating the server and routes. By the end, you'll have a working API endpoint that fetches and combines user and order data, demonstrating a common pattern for improving frontend performance.
intro.usecase: In modern web applications, the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern is essential for aggregating data from multiple microservices into a single optimized response. This is commonly seen in e-commerce product pages where a BFF endpoint combines product details, inventory status, pricing, and customer reviews from separate services. Similarly, dashboard applications use BFF endpoints to fetch and merge data from analytics, user management, and reporting services into a unified view. By implementing this pattern, developers reduce frontend complexity, minimize network requests, and improve application performance.
